q: Normal form theory reduces a vector field near a bifurcation to its simplest equivalent form. The normal form for the Hopf bifurcation (in polar coordinates) is:
opts: ṙ = μr − r³, θ̇ = ω + br² (supercritical)
exp: Supercritical Hopf normal form: ṙ = μr − r³, θ̇ = ω + br². For μ < 0: stable focus at origin; for μ > 0: unstable focus and stable limit cycle of radius √μ. The cubic term (first Lyapunov coefficient) determines super- vs. subcritical.
